title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 6
statement: Emmy says to Max, “I ordered \(36\) math club sweatshirts today.” Max asks, “How much did each shirt cost?” Emmy responds, “I’ll give you a hint. The total cost was \(\$\underline{A}\,\underline{B}\,\underline{B}.\underline{B}\,\underline{A},\) where \(A\) and \(B\) are digits and \(A \neq 0.\)” After a pause, Max says, “That was a good price.” What is \(A + B?\)

solutions.text:
The total in cents is \(10000A + 1110B + A\) \(= 10001A + 1110B,\) which must be a multiple of \(36.\) Since \(10001 \equiv 29\) and \(1110 \equiv 30 \pmod{36},\) the condition is \(29A + 30B \equiv 0,\) i.e. \(7A + 6B \equiv 0 \pmod{36}.\) Reducing once more modulo \(6\) gives \(A\equiv0\pmod6,\) so the only possible nonzero digit is \(A=6.\) Then \(42+6B\) is divisible by \(36\) only for the digit \(B=5.\) Indeed \(\$655.56 = 36 \times \$18.21,\) so \(A+B=11.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: In cents the total is \(10001A + 1110B,\) and it must be divisible by \(36\)
Reduce modulo \(36\) to get \(7A + 6B \equiv 0,\) then test digits with \(A \neq 0\)
